messages:
maria_support: Hey team, customer (alice_customer) is seeing partial streaming responses when they go through a gateway. Works fine direct to our hosted API, but when routed via their HTTP/1.1 proxy (Envoy->Nginx) the SSE stream either stalls or returns a truncated final event. They say client reconnects sometimes get the last token duplicated. Escalating. 

alice_customer: FYI reproducer: node-fetch to https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream with request-id header. Repro steps below. Happens ~60% of the time when the path crosses HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 translation at the gateway.

jgonzalez: thanks. can you paste the exact curl/h2 commands and response shapes? also what's the model and prompt size?

alice_customer: model=redwood-stream-2, prompt ~= 400 tokens. Example (simplified):

```
# http/2 client (works)
curl -v --http2 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Request-Id: xy-123" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-stream-2","input":"hello"}' \n  https://internal.upstream:8443/v1/stream
```

```
# through gateway (fails intermittently)
curl -v --http1.1 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Request-Id: xy-123" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-stream-2","input":"hello"}' \n  https://proxy.company.example/stream
```

In the failing case client sees a chunk like: `data: {"token":"foo","done":false}` then nothing for 10s then a final `data: {"token":"bar","done":true}` but our logs show tokens in between. Looks like the proxy buffered multiple SSE events and shipped them all at once or sometimes closed early.

sree_infra: that pattern screams proxy buffering or HTTP/1.1 chunk coalescing. Which gateway are they running? nginx with proxy_buffering on? Envoy filter chain? Also need tcpdump or HAR to confirm wire frames.

alice_customer: Envoy (h2->h2 to us) fronting, then NGINX (h2->http1) to some internal service. They said disabling proxy_buffering in nginx helped once.

jgonzalez: OK. Quick theory: when HTTP/2 upstream sends small DATA frames for each SSE event, the HTTP/1.1 bridge might buffer until a threshold or until connection close before flushing. With SSE we rely on timely flushes. Nginx has proxy_buffering on by default; Envoy may also buffer when doing http2 to http1 conversion. Also some CDNs will re-chunk.

harry_prod: also check for headers that force buffering: Content-Length present? If the gateway rewrites or adds Content-Length it will buffer until complete. For chunked streaming you must not set Content-Length and ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked is preserved or the bridge flushes per chunk.

maria_support: action items for debugging (quick list):
- collect curl -v --http2 and curl -v --http1.1 outputs from the customer (include full request/response headers)
- ask gateway admin to capture nginx/conf and envoy config for http2 to http1 translation (look for proxy_buffering, proxy_http_version, sendfile, tcp_nodelay, http2_body_prio)
- request tcpdump or wireshark to see h2 frames vs h1 chunk boundaries (we want to know whether SSE events are split at wire level or merged)
- reproduce locally: run an h2 upstream that emits SSE every 100ms and run an nginx instance with default buffering to see behavior
- get HAR or browser devtools when client is a browser

sree_infra: repro script idea (shareable):
```
# tiny HTTP/2 server that streams SSE
python3 -u -m http.server 8443 --bind 0.0.0.0  # (pseudo) use an h2 server lib in reality
# or use node http2 with res.stream.write('data: ...\n\n') every 100ms
```
Then proxy with nginx default conf and with `proxy_buffering off;` and compare. Also try `add_header X-Accel-Buffering no;` for nginx. For Envoy, set `use_remote_address` and check `stream_idle_timeout` and buffer limits on `http_connection_manager`.

alice_customer: they also saw reconnect duplication: when client reconnects for resume we sometimes re-send last token. Client is implementing a naive resume by last event id. There might be race where the proxy closed without forwarding the final ack so customer retried and got a partial duplicate.

jgonzalez: for dedupe on reconnect, recommend server-side idempotency using event IDs and dedupe at client if possible. We can also include a `final_event_id` header once stream completes so client can reconcile. However primary goal is to avoid buffering.

maria_support: suggested temporary mitigations to try for the customer:
- set `proxy_buffering off;` in NGINX for the SSE path or add `X-Accel-Buffering: no` in responses
- ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` is preserved; avoid `Content-Length` insertion
- if using Cloudflare/ALB, try bypassing or put the route in a passthrough mode; some CDNs force buffering
- as fallback, use WebSocket-based streaming instead of SSE if the intermediary messes with chunking

deploy-bot: deploy success: nginx config patch applied to staging with proxy_buffering=off for /stream  (ci/deploy/3421) :white_check_mark:

alice_customer: we patched nginx `proxy_buffering off` and it looks much better. Still seeing rare stalls (~1%). Attached logs and a tcpdump.

sree_infra: looking at tcpdump: I can see small HTTP/1.1 chunks arriving grouped by NGINX into larger TCP segments, but NGINX did flush when app wrote. The remaining 1% might be due to keepalive reuse causing coalescing; try `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ''; proxy_set_header Proxy-Connection ''; proxy_buffering off; proxy_ignore_client_abort off;` and `sendfile off;`

jgonzalez: also confirm no mutating middleware (gzip, response buffering modules) are present. Set `gzip off` for SSE route. Add `Cache-Control: no-transform` to response to avoid intermediaries altering chunking.

maria_support: summarizing for support ticket:
- root cause: intermediary (HTTP/2->HTTP/1) buffering and chunk coalescing leading to delayed SSE flushes and occasional truncated/duplicated events on reconnects
- repro: reproduce with h2 upstream emitting frequent small SSE messages + nginx/Envoy default proxying; toggling `proxy_buffering` demonstrates difference
- mitigation: disable proxy buffering, preserve chunked encoding, add X-Accel-Buffering: no, use no-transform, or switch to WebSocket fallback. For long-term, recommend end-to-end HTTP/2 where possible or ensure gateway supports streaming flush semantics.

alice_customer: thanks — will roll nginx change to prod behind a feature flag and report back over next 24h. Appreciate the escalated help. :pray:

maria_support: thanks everyone. If they still see issues collect HAR, tcpdump, and attach `Request-Id` header values so we can trace server logs. Closing this thread for now, will reopen if customer reports more. :eyes:
